definition: The number of full-time equivalent (FTE) employees engaged in the utility's distribution function for the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll, converted to full-time equivalents (two half-time staff = 1 FTE); exclude contractors and consultants. Feeds the Customers per Distribution Employee KPI. Report FTE, not headcount — a part-time employee counts as a fraction of an FTE.

The number of full-time equivalent (FTE) employees engaged in the utility's generation function for the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll, converted to full-time equivalents (two half-time staff = 1 FTE); exclude contractors and consultants. Feeds the Generation Labor Productivity KPI. Staff who split their time across functions should be apportioned so that each person's FTE is counted only once across divisions.

The number of full-time equivalent (FTE) employees engaged in the utility's transmission function for the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll, converted to full-time equivalents (two half-time staff = 1 FTE); exclude contractors and consultants. Utilities that do not operate a separate transmission network should leave this blank rather than repeating distribution staff here.

The number of female employees working in the utility's administrative division, reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the Administrative Employees Female %, Administrative Employees Total, Total Employees Female and IPP Generation KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure — count each person once regardless of hours worked.

The number of male employees working in the utility's administrative division, reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the Administrative Employees Male %, Administrative Employees Total and Total Employees Male KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure — count each person once regardless of hours worked.

The total number of employees in the utility's administrative division, in employees. It is calculated automatically as the sum of the reported male and female administrative employee counts, so no separate entry is required. Feeds the Administrative Employees Female % and Administrative Employees Male % KPIs. If the total looks wrong, correct the underlying male and female counts rather than this value.

The total number of female employees across the whole utility, in employees. It is calculated by summing the female headcounts reported for each division (executive, technical, finance, procurement, human resources, PR/marketing/customer service, administrative, ICT and other), so no separate entry is required. Feeds the Employees Female % and Total Employees KPIs, which underpin the PPA's utility-wide gender-representation reporting. Ensure each employee is assigned to exactly one division so this total does not double-count anyone.

The total number of male employees across the whole utility, in employees. It is calculated by summing the male headcounts reported for each division (executive, technical, finance, procurement, human resources, PR/marketing/customer service, administrative, ICT and other), so no separate entry is required. Feeds the Employees Male % and Total Employees KPIs, which underpin the PPA's utility-wide gender-representation reporting. Ensure each employee is assigned to exactly one division so this total does not double-count anyone.

The number of female employees in the utility's executive division (the senior leadership team), reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants, board members who are not employees, and vacant positions. Feeds the Executive Employees Female %, Executive Employees Total and Total Employees Female KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

The number of male employees in the utility's executive division (the senior leadership team), reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants, board members who are not employees, and vacant positions. Feeds the Executive Employees Male %, Executive Employees Total and Total Employees Male KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. The total number of employees in the utility's executive division (the senior leadership team), in employees. The total number of employees in the utility's finance division, in employees. Records the gender of the utility's second-in-command — typically the Deputy CEO, Chief Operating Officer or most senior executive reporting directly to the CEO — as at the end of the reporting year; this is a gender value, not a number. Report the person actually occupying the role at year end, including an acting incumbent if the position is filled in an acting capacity. Feeds the Gender of Utility 2nd in command KPI, part of the PPA's reporting of gender representation in utility leadership.

Records the gender of the utility's Chief Executive Officer (or equivalent most senior executive, such as a General Manager) as at the end of the reporting year; this is a gender value, not a number. Report the person actually occupying the role at year end, including an acting CEO if the position is filled in an acting capacity. Feeds the Gender of Utility CEO KPI, part of the PPA's reporting of gender representation in utility leadership.

The number of female employees in divisions not covered by the named categories (executive, technical, finance, procurement, human resources, PR/marketing/customer service, administrative and ICT), reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions, and do not repeat anyone already counted in a named division. Feeds the Other Divisions Employees Female %, Other Divisions Employees Total and Total Employees Female KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

The number of male employees in divisions not covered by the named categories (executive, technical, finance, procurement, human resources, PR/marketing/customer service, administrative and ICT), reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions, and do not repeat anyone already counted in a named division. Feeds the Other Divisions Employees Male %, Other Divisions Employees Total and Total Employees Male KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

The total number of employees in divisions not covered by the named categories (executive, technical, finance, procurement, human resources, PR/marketing/customer service, administrative and ICT), in employees. It is calculated as the sum of the reported male and female counts for these other divisions, so no separate entry is required. Feeds the Other Divisions Employees Female % and Other Divisions Employees Male % KPIs. If the total looks wrong, correct the underlying male and female counts rather than this value.

The number of female employees in the utility's public relations, marketing and customer service division, reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. Include permanent full-time and part-time employees on the utility's payroll, including call-centre and front-counter customer service staff; exclude contractors, consultants and vacant positions. Feeds the PR Marketing and CustService Employees Female %, PR Marketing and CustService Employees Total and Total Employees Female KPIs, and supports the PPA's reporting of gender representation by division. This is a headcount, not an FTE figure.

The total number of employees in the utility's public relations, marketing and customer service division, in employees. It is calculated as the sum of the reported male and female counts for this division, so no separate entry is required. Feeds the PR Marketing and CustService Employees Female % and PR Marketing and CustService Employees Male % KPIs. The number of female employees in the utility's technical division (engineering, generation, network operations and similar technical roles), reported as a headcount of employees at the end of the reporting year. The total number of scheduled work hours lost during the reporting year because of work-related injuries, in hours. Count hours that the utility's own employees were rostered to work but could not because of a lost-time injury; exclude contractor injuries and absences unrelated to workplace injury. Feeds the Lost Time Injury Duration Rate KPI. Include hours lost during the reporting year even where the injury itself occurred in an earlier year.

The number of work-related injury incidents recorded during the reporting year, in incidents. Count injuries to the utility's own employees arising out of or in the course of work that resulted in lost work time; exclude contractor injuries and first-aid-only cases that caused no lost time. Feeds the Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate KPI. Record each qualifying incident once, in the year it occurred.

The total number of hours paid to employees in the utility's distribution division during the reporting year, in hours. Include all remunerated hours for employees on the utility's payroll — ordinary time, overtime and paid leave such as annual and sick leave; exclude contractor hours. Feeds the FTE Paid Hours - Distribution and FTE Worked Hours - Distribution KPIs. Paid hours are normally higher than worked hours because they include paid leave and public holidays.

The total number of hours paid to employees in the utility's other electrical functions — electrical activities outside generation, transmission and distribution — during the reporting year, in hours. Include all remunerated hours for employees on the utility's payroll — ordinary time, overtime and paid leave such as annual and sick leave; exclude contractor hours. Feeds the FTE Paid Hours - Other Electrical KPI. Paid hours are normally higher than worked hours because they include paid leave and public holidays.

The total number of hours paid to employees in the utility's transmission division during the reporting year, in hours. Include all remunerated hours for employees on the utility's payroll — ordinary time, overtime and paid leave such as annual and sick leave; exclude contractor hours. Feeds the FTE Paid Hours - Transmission and FTE Worked Hours - Transmission KPIs. Paid hours are normally higher than worked hours because they include paid leave and public holidays.

The total number of hours actually worked by employees in the utility's distribution division during the reporting year, in hours. Include ordinary time and overtime actually worked by employees on the utility's payroll; exclude paid leave, public holidays and contractor hours. Feeds the FTE Worked Hours - Distribution KPI and the Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate. Do not report paid hours here — leave and holidays are paid but not worked.

The total number of hours actually worked by employees in the utility's other electrical functions — electrical activities outside generation, transmission and distribution — during the reporting year, in hours. Include ordinary time and overtime actually worked by employees on the utility's payroll; exclude paid leave, public holidays and contractor hours. Feeds the FTE Worked Hours - Other Electrical KPI and the Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate. Do not report paid hours here — leave and holidays are paid but not worked.

The total number of hours actually worked by employees in the utility's transmission division during the reporting year, in hours. Include ordinary time and overtime actually worked by employees on the utility's payroll; exclude paid leave, public holidays and contractor hours. Feeds the FTE Worked Hours - Transmission KPI. Do not report paid hours here — leave and holidays are paid but not worked.

The standard annual work hours for one full-time employee in the utility's distribution division, in hours. Report the contracted or rostered hours a single full-time employee is expected to work in the year (for example, standard weekly hours multiplied by the number of working weeks), not the division-wide total and not hours actually worked or paid. Feeds the FTE Paid Hours - Distribution and FTE Worked Hours - Distribution KPIs, where it is the divisor that converts total hours into FTEs. A common error is entering the division's total hours instead of the per-employee standard.

The standard annual work hours for one full-time employee in the utility's other electrical functions — electrical activities outside generation, transmission and distribution — in hours. Report the contracted or rostered hours a single full-time employee is expected to work in the year (for example, standard weekly hours multiplied by the number of working weeks), not the function-wide total and not hours actually worked or paid. Feeds the FTE Paid Hours - Other Electrical and FTE Worked Hours - Other Electrical KPIs, where it is the divisor that converts total hours into FTEs. A common error is entering the total hours for the function instead of the per-employee standard.

Report the contracted or rostered hours a single full-time employee is expected to work in the year (for example, standard weekly hours multiplied by the number of working weeks), not the division-wide total and not hours actually worked or paid.
